headline: LTX-2.5 generates 10-second AI video from image in 6.8s on Nvidia superchips, with open weights.
summary: LTX-2.5, the new open-weights video and "world" model, can create a 10-second video from an image in just 6.8 seconds on high-end hardware. It's now integrated into ComfyUI and available on Hugging Face.
details: LTX, a company spun out of Lightricks, has released LTX-2.5, its newest open-weights video and "world" model. It can generate a 10-second, 720p image-to-video clip in just 6.8 seconds on two NVIDIA GB200 chips. The model is natively integrated into ComfyUI.

LTX-2.5 is available as open weights on Hugging Face, within ComfyUI, and via the LTX API. It is free for organizations with under $10 million in annual recurring revenue, with larger companies requiring a license. The LTX family has surpassed 33 million downloads.

The new version rebuilds nearly every stage of the generation pipeline. Key improvements include a new diffusion video decoder for better quality, native multishot generation for consistent sequences, and a custom Gemma 4 language backbone for complex prompts. It also offers a pretrained checkpoint for physical AI and robotics.

LTX claims its model offers roughly one-eighth the cost and one-seventh the render time of comparable models. It runs on hardware ranging from data center GPUs down to a Mac, requiring a minimum of 16GB of VRAM.

While the 6.8-second speed is on top-end NVIDIA GB200 chips, the same job via LTX's managed API takes 23.7 seconds for a 1080p resolution. This compares favorably to other APIs, with Google's Gemini Omni Flash at 52 seconds and xAI's Grok 1.5 at 63 seconds for similar tasks.

In blind human preference tests, LTX-2.5 achieved a 67% win rate for video quality, slightly ahead of ByteDance's Seedance 2.5. These results are vendor-reported and preliminary, intended as directional claims.
The model offers deployment flexibility, running on-premises, at the edge, or via API, with no mandatory branding on output. It can also be fine-tuned on a customer's own data and IP.

headline_marked: Nvidia's Switchyard router [[cuts AI task costs to a third]] by reshuffling models mid-task
headline: Nvidia's Switchyard router cuts AI task costs to a third by reshuffling models mid-task
summary: Nvidia's new open-source NeMo Switchyard library, paired with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, can reduce AI agent task costs by two-thirds while maintaining frontier-level performance.
details: Nvidia has launched NeMo Switchyard, an open-source library designed to dynamically route AI agent tasks to the most suitable models, significantly reducing operational costs. Paired with the new Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter open mixture-of-experts model, the system reportedly cuts benchmark costs to roughly a third of running a single frontier model.

Enterprises often face a dilemma: use expensive frontier models for all tasks or build complex custom routing for cheaper models. Switchyard aims to solve this by intelligently directing each step of an agent workflow, adapting to changing task states and tool returns.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning itself offers impressive speed, delivering up to 4x faster output than comparable models and completing agentic tasks about 30% faster than Qwen3.6-35B at similar accuracy levels.

The system's intelligence allows it to evaluate factors like a model's verbosity (tokens produced) to steer work towards cheaper options before a call is made. This dynamic routing ensures optimal resource allocation, preventing overspending on simpler tasks.

Switchyard is designed for integration, plugging into existing LLM gateways like Kong, LiteLLM, and OpenRouter, and partnering with agent frameworks such as LangChain. Nvidia emphasizes an 'ecosystem lover' approach, ensuring broad compatibility rather than outright replacement of current solutions.
